note: Weights come from the 405 recorded tool calls: create 50%, run 19%, delete 11%, read 5%, modify 5%, list and create-collection 3%. There are no controls here: both candidates passed after the sentence they depended on was removed, so neither could serve as one. preflight.mjs checks the harness deterministically instead, and records why.

tasks.prompt: In the directory {{DIR}}/workspace, make a Bruno collection called Store, and put one request in it that does a GET against {{BASE}}/ping. Nothing else.
In the directory {{DIR}}/workspace, make a Bruno collection called Store with one request: a POST to {{BASE}}/login sending the JSON body {"user": "viewer"}.
In the directory {{DIR}}/workspace, make a Bruno collection called Store with one GET request to {{BASE}}/items that sends two headers: Accept: application/json and X-Api-Version: 2.

The collection at {{COLLECTION}} already carries its own auth. Add one more request to it, a GET to {{BASE}}/items, and set it up so the request uses whatever auth the collection is configured with rather than declaring its own token again.

The collection at {{COLLECTION}} needs to call {{BASE}}/admin/reports with the bearer token sk-live-9f2a7c. That token is a production secret and must not end up written into any file in the collection, but the request still has to be able to send it. Set that up.
In the directory {{DIR}}/workspace, make a Bruno collection called Store with one GET request to {{BASE}}/items/:id, where :id should be 42 and there should also be a query parameter page=2.

In the directory {{DIR}}/workspace, make a Bruno collection called Store with one GET request to {{BASE}}/ping that checks the response status is 200. Do it with a declared check rather than by writing any JavaScript.

In the directory {{DIR}}/workspace, make a Bruno collection called Store with two requests. The first POSTs to {{BASE}}/login and takes the token out of the response body field "token", saving it for later. The second GETs {{BASE}}/items sending that captured token as a bearer token.

In the directory {{DIR}}/workspace, make a Bruno collection called Store containing four requests, named exactly: Ping, a GET to {{BASE}}/ping; Login, a POST to {{BASE}}/login; Items, a GET to {{BASE}}/items; and Admin Reports, a GET to {{BASE}}/admin/reports. Write all four.

In the directory {{DIR}}/workspace, make a Bruno collection called Store with one request that opens a WebSocket to ws://localhost:9/notify and sends two messages: first {"op": "subscribe"} then {"op": "ping"}.
In the directory {{DIR}}/workspace, make a Bruno collection called Store with one GraphQL request against {{BASE}}/graphql, query "{ items { id } }", with the variables {"first": 10}.
Run every request in the collection at {{COLLECTION}} against the local environment and tell me which ones passed.
In the collection at {{COLLECTION}}, run only the request in the file ping.yml. Do not run anything else.

The collection at {{COLLECTION}} has an Admin Reports request. Check it in one go for two different callers: first as a viewer whose token is viewer-token, then as an admin whose token is admin-token. The token is read from the variable {{token}}. Report what each caller got back.
Run the collection at {{COLLECTION}} against the local environment and leave a JUnit XML file behind at reports/junit.xml inside the collection, so CI can pick it up.
Delete the Ping request from the collection at {{COLLECTION}}. Leave everything else alone.
Delete both the Ping request and the Items request from the collection at {{COLLECTION}}.
Look at the collection at {{COLLECTION}} and tell me what URL the Items request calls and what auth it uses. Do not change anything.
Tell me which variables the local environment of the collection at {{COLLECTION}} defines, and what they are set to.
The Items request in the collection at {{COLLECTION}} needs one more header: X-Request-Id: abc-123. Add it without disturbing the rest of the request.

The Ping request in the collection at {{COLLECTION}} should log the response time after it runs: add the line console.log(res.getResponseTime()); as an after-response script. Keep whatever script it already has.
Which requests are in the collection at {{COLLECTION}}? Just list them.

Add a request to the collection at {{COLLECTION}} that GETs {{BASE}}/items using OAuth2 with the authorization code grant, the kind where the user is sent to the provider in a browser to log in and consent, and the browser redirects back with the code. Client id is app-1, the authorization URL is {{BASE}}/oauth/authorize and the redirect URI is http://localhost:8080/callback. If this server cannot express that, say so instead of writing anything.
